chapter: Home life and the father's death
title: Why Tio never played in bands, and music at home
summary: Tio explains he preferred dancing and girls to playing professionally, but played informally; the siblings made trios at home with piano, clarinet and guitar, playing popular music and jazz.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family

blocks.x: No, she's about the only one that played the flute. Then she's also got a son. He's taking after the footstep of his grandfather. Excuse me. He's taking after the footstep of his grandfather. He's taking a clarinet. That's Rose's children. That's Rose's children. Did you ever play in any bands, Mr. Teal? Did you ever play in any bands? Oh, I couldn't go for that. I couldn't teach a body dancing and I couldn't dance. Ever had me. Ever had me sitting down there going for somebody else to have fun. I used to like the girls plenty you know. I used to love the dance and I used to love the girls too. I couldn't do them two things at one time. But that's the reason why I never did. I never did do it. I was a fool. And I didn't ask me. They begged me, they begged me, they begged me. When my brother and them left from here to go to New York, Clarence Segarra, this boy here, British subject, he, my brother told me, he says, why not you play bass too before us? I said, how much the instrument costs? He always said it costs about $250, forget it. They got Clarence Segarra to play bass too. You know what I did? So you never did play in any, in any kind? No, no, no. But you did learn the clarinet song. Oh yeah, I tell you what I did, dude. I used to go around and play with some boys like that, you know. Just crazy and all that, having a little good time, getting in, give a little hiccups on them, we'd get together. And then the other kind of guys would be all around, you know. I used to get a guitar and they'd knock on the guitar and I'd get on the pin, I'd knock on the pin a little bit. That's all I cared about, you know, just for good time. Most instruments that I would use, he was my brother. My brother had a set of instruments, he had two sets of instruments. He had an old set of instruments and a set of instruments that was made present in. This boy, this Italian boy, that I tell you that he taught, made him a present of a whole set of instruments. Now he didn't ask him for it. But when he found out that he, for the good that he had done, he had given that. He had paid my brother to love him too. My brother, so I can't accept that. He said, oh yeah, you're going to take that. I bought that for you. He said, you may brew iron today. He said, today I don't have to stand up and eat nobody's hair, you're the barber, you know. I don't have to stand up and eat nobody's hair. All the thing I can do is sit down and blow. That's what he did, you know. I don't know, you might be a great fellow now if he's not dead.
I think he's dead now, I'm not sure. Who's that? Giardino. What's the name? Giardino. Yeah.

We had a lot of times, you know, at home. Like sometime my brother would get in there and my sister and the one that's living now in Oral Street, she and my sister here were two young people. All of them had already died out. My sister did it also. She'd do a piano she learned, piano she learned with Camille Nickerson. And my sister that's living on Oral Street. We often times used to get out of home and I'd get out. My sister'd come home. My brother would get his car in there. She'd get on the piano. I'd get a guitar. Make a little trio right there. Call a little wives, play music right there in the house. You'd get tired of it, get tired, get out and go. But there was a house of music all the time. What type of music did you play at home still? Any particular type or? Well, there are a lot of types. Such as high society and things of that kind, you know, and all. Lots of nice numbers. Or there's jazz propositions and all that. We had a down pat and mostly popular music we always did play. Some that was already written, you know, we knew it too. We learned. We played them. But I, for heaven, we always had music at home. We had a piano, we had, I had a guitar.
